title: Objects
objective: Create objects, read and change their properties, write methods and work with arrays of objects
story: We've docked at a space station in the nebula. The officer asks for the ship's ID card: its name, speed, fuel, crew... The way to keep information that belongs together in a single package is an **object**.

sections.title: Objects: keys and values
sections.body:
An object is written with curly braces and holds `key: value` pairs. You reach the values with a **dot** or **square brackets**:

```js
const ship = {
  name: "Eagle",
  speed: 40000,
  crew: ["Alex", "Ada"],
};

console.log(ship.name);        // Eagle
console.log(ship["speed"]);    // 40000
const key = "crew";
console.log(ship[key]);        // ['Alex', 'Ada']

ship.speed = 45000;            // change
ship.color = "silver";         // add a new key
delete ship.color;             // delete a key
```

If the key is inside a variable, square brackets are a must: `ship[key]`. Reading a key that doesn't exist gives `undefined`. If you know Python: an object is like a dictionary (dict).

sections.title: Methods and this
Walking through objects
sections.body:
| Code | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `Object.keys(ship)` | An array of keys: `['name', 'speed']` |
| `Object.values(ship)` | An array of values: `['Eagle', 40000]` |
| `Object.entries(ship)` | An array of pairs: `[['name', 'Eagle'], ['speed', 40000]]` |

`for...in` walks through an object's keys in turn:

```js
for (const key in ship) {
  console.log(key, "→", ship[key]);
}
```

Don't mix them up: `for...of` for arrays, `for...in` for an object's keys.

tasks.title: Planet card
tasks.prompt:
1. Create an object called `planet`: `name` `"Mars"`, `moons` `2`, `color` `"red"`.
2. **After** creating the object, add a new key with a dot: `visited` `true`.
3. Read the values with dots and print this line: `Mars: 2 moons, red`
hints: Use values like ${planet.name} in a template string.

tasks.title: Info reader
tasks.prompt:
Work with the `ship` object:

- `value`: the value of the key stored in the `field` variable. Use square brackets: `ship[field]`
- `keyCount`: how many keys does the object have? (`Object.keys`)
- With a `for...in` loop, print every key and its value as `key: value` (like `name: Eagle`).
hints: Object.keys(ship) gives an array; its length is .length

tasks.title: Rocket methods
tasks.prompt:
Add two methods to the `rocket` object:

- `refuel(amount)`: adds `amount` to `this.fuel`, but fuel **must not go over 100**; returns the new fuel.
- `status()`: returns a text like `Eagle: fuel 80` (the name and fuel must be read with `this`).
hints: Writing a method: refuel(amount) { ... }, (don't forget the comma between them)

challenge.title: Crew report
challenge.prompt:
The `crewReport(list)` function takes an array of crew members and returns this object:

- `totalHours`: the sum of everyone's flight hours
- `pilots`: the names of those whose role is `"pilot"` (an array)
- `veteran`: the name of the person with the most flight hours

Use **destructuring** in the loop: `for (const { name, role, hours } of list)`. Try your function with a different crew too.
hints: Before the loop: let totalHours = 0; const pilots = []; let veteran = ""; let maxHours = -1;
When you see bigger hours, update maxHours and veteran.
The short form: return { totalHours, pilots, veteran };

project_task.title: Player object
project_task.prompt:
Let's collect all of the player's info in one `player` object. The starting info is ready; add these three methods:

- `collectStar()`: adds 1 to `stars` and returns the new number of stars.
- `hit()`: takes 1 from `lives` but **never below 0**; returns the lives left.
- `status()`: returns a text like `Eagle | Stars: 2 | Lives: 2` (with `this`).

The ready-made lines below let the player collect 2 stars, get hit once and print the status.
